messages:
jamie: heads up for people doing localserve in docker: i kept losing auth after a few requests. host redwoodctl refreshes but container stays anon.

ria: are you mounting the cache dir? ~/.redwood -> /home/dev/.redwood?

jamie: yup. example: -v ~/.redwood:/home/dev/.redwood:ro. i was mounting read-only because i don't want containers mutating my host cache.

kevin: ro mount means the container can't write refreshed tokens. older CLIs will try to update cache and silently fail. that explains the 401s.

jamie: ah. so what do folks do for ephemeral CI/local tests without rebuilding images?

ria: two patterns that worked for us: 1) run a small auth-proxy sidecar on host that exposes a local auth endpoint and point REDWOOD_AUTH_URL at it, so containers can request fresh tokens without writing host files; 2) inject a short-lived REDWOOD_TOKEN env var when starting container for single-run jobs.

kevin: note: also watch UID/GID mismatches. if files are owned by a different uid and container user can't write, redwoodctl will log a cache write error but currently it's pretty subtle. we should add clearer warnings.

jamie: can we add a CLI flag to explicitly run in "container mode" where it does non-file-based refresh/polling?

kevin: there's an open WIP to add `redwoodctl auth refresh --non-interactive` and a `--no-filewatch` toggle. i'll link the PR.

devex-bot: Created DE-2456: "redwoodctl: container-friendly auth mode + clearer cache permission diagnostics"

ria: short doc blurb i'll add to localserve: explain mount perms, env-token quickstart, and auth-proxy pattern. also add troubleshooting checklist (binary parity, filewatch inode caveats, uid/gid).

jamie: perfect. thx — saved me a day. :tada:
